pool.text: Étienne Brûlé became the first documented European to navigate the Ottawa River.
Wright founded a lumber town north of the river in Hull.
A town was established and later named after Colonel John By.
The Rideau Canal first opened to serve as a major waterway route.
Bypassing small settlements, Bytown grew as the Rideau Canal was completed.
The Ottawa Citizen was established as the Bytown Packet newspaper.
King George VI made his first visit to his parliament in Ottawa.
Carleton University was founded to meet the needs of returning veterans.
VE Day was marked with a large celebration across the city.
The very first raising of Canada's new national flag took place.
The entire length of Sparks Street was turned into a pedestrian mall.
Algonquin College was founded as a college of applied arts and technology.
The Region of Ottawa-Carleton was formed from eleven townships and municipalities.
The National Arts Centre opened as a major performing arts venue.
Ottawa Race Weekend began hosting participants during the fourth weekend of May.
Ottawa hosted the Kitchen Accord negotiations for the Canadian constitution.
Queen Elizabeth II issued a royal proclamation for the Constitution Act.
A campus located off the Aviation Parkway in Carson Meadows was founded.
Notre Dame Cathedral Basilica was designated as a National Historic Site.
Civil servants transitioned to online work due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
